# Pathway: Carousel

Everything the Brain knows that applies to **Carousel**, in the order you'd use it. 124 ideas. Niche sections list only the extra, niche-specific ideas. [index](../index.md)


## Idea

- **[Yap Map: 3–5 ideas a day](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-yap-map)**: Use dead time to log 3–5 ideas a day in a notes app from your day's touch points, personal life, media you consume and shower/workout thoughts; give each one a take.
- **[Idea faucets: Reddit and your own winners](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-reddit-faucet)**: Sort your niche subreddit by top of the month and have ChatGPT summarise what people discuss; and turn last week's most viral video into one specific buzzword ("creative tax strategies") for next week's video.
- **[Shareability: why would they send it?](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-shareability-test)**: The key test is whether someone would send it to someone else (relatable, expertise, tutorial, funny, interesting, beautiful). Our playbook ranks sends per reach as the strongest signal for reaching new people.
- **[Pick one goal: comments, sends or saves](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-conversation-goal)**: Decide whether a video is for comments, sends (communal language like "me and the boys after we ___") or saves; you usually can't hit all of them.
- **[AI prompt: unique, specific, observed](../topics/ai-tools.md#ideas-unique-specific-observed)**: Use AI for ideation: ask for the most unique, specific and observed situation your ideal viewer has lived. Name the problem nobody has named (Briar's "follower quality" drew "Finally, someone's talking about…"). ⚠ C22
- **[Ideas from DM and comment questions](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-questions-not-polls)**: Best ideas come from DM and comment questions, not "what should I make?" polls; ~5 people asking the same thing means thousands have it. Topic test: passionate? resonates now? most of all, will it change their actions?
- **[Community content: involve, converse, showcase](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-as-hero)**: Let the audience pick between two versions, share their wins publicly, stitch their stories (even 300-follower accounts). Three pillars: educational, conversational, social proof.
- **[Photos of real objects (post-it, printed quote)](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-real-world-photos)**: Photos of real-world things (a post-it, a printed quote poster, a hand drawing) were performing well as posts (Feb 2025).
- **[Content hackathon: make 1–2 wild pieces](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-hackathon)**: Monthly or quarterly: a safe-space kickoff, each person makes 1–2 new pieces that will crush or flop (9 a.m.–4 p.m.), presentations explaining why, team votes, the winner runs publicly. Reward innovation, not performance.
- **[Brand = intentional pairing, done consistently](../topics/brand.md#brand-intentional-pairing)**: Branding is a pairing of things; good branding is an intentional pairing of relevant things done consistently; brand is the audience's resulting association (Nike + Jordan, Harley + freedom).
- **[Decide what not to be associated with](../topics/brand.md#brand-anti-associations)**: The more important question: what do you NOT want to be associated with (collabs, podcasts, sponsors)? He'd decline even the biggest audience.
- **[Brand Journey: work backwards](../topics/brand.md#brand-journey-backwards)**: Desired outcome → what you must be known for → what you must do → what you must learn (the last gives day-one actions).
- **[Own the gap: what do you disagree with?](../topics/brand.md#brand-own-the-gap)**: Positioning = find the gap: what are creators in your space saying that you disagree with, and how can you bring a fresh perspective to old teaching?
- **[Brand story: catalyst, core truth, proof](../topics/brand.md#brand-story-catalyst-truth-proof)**: Catalyst (why it exists), core truth (what you believe that others don't, not controversy for its own sake), proof (what you do and prove over and over).
- **[Start narrow, expand in layers](../topics/brand.md#brand-start-narrow-layers)**: Early trust comes from being great at one specific thing; expand only into adjacent topics, once excellent, after consistent engagement or when the audience asks, keeping your roots. ⚠ C19
- **[80/20 interest stacking](../topics/brand.md#brand-interest-stacking)**: 80% your core subject, 20% other interests; each extra interest is another "at bat" to connect. Pillars are guidelines, not rules.
- **[Positioning: known for, shelf test](../topics/brand.md#brand-positioning-known-for)**: Positioning is what you're known for: not generic, remembered, AI-legible. Shelf test: stand next to everyone in the category and name your reason to exist (Monster = counterculture, Celsius = health).
- **[Positioning type and one statement](../topics/brand.md#brand-positioning-types)**: Pick one type (performance, category creation, counter, smart, value, niche, generational, single attribute, premium, counter-luxury, name) as north star; write "For [target] who [need], [brand] is the [category] that [benefit]. Unlike [competitor], we [differentiator]."
- **[Brand world: characters, sets, plot](../topics/brand.md#brand-world-characters-sets)**: Map who can be on camera and every set, then plot it like TV: events, enemies (competitor moves), friends (partners to piggyback), specials (your own series for empty stretches); find the holes and refresh monthly.
- **[Events calendar: personal, culture, industry](../topics/brand.md#brand-events-calendar)**: A calendar by month or quarter of company/personal events, culture moments (New Year, summer, Black Friday) and industry events (CES, competitor launches).
- **[Brand = a title plus one emotion](../topics/brand.md#brand-title-one-emotion)**: Tombstone test: what one title would people give you, and can they attach one emotion (Nike = hard work, New Balance = style)?
- **[Counter-position = different, not opposite](../topics/brand.md#brand-counter-position-different)**: Counter-positioning means different positioning, not opposite; spike into a pocket, then grow out (Amazon with books, Vans with skaters).
- **[Small right audience beats big wrong one](../topics/brand.md#brand-follower-quality)**: How and on what you grow is what your audience will always be; 10,000 quality followers can change your life. Caleb's 68K landscape-photo followers don't engage with his current topic.
- **[Positioning: what do you replace?](../topics/brand.md#brand-what-do-you-replace)**: "You're going to need a smaller cabinet": name what you replace; and what can you do that no one else does that people care about (The Secret Footballer, Loom's "async video").
- **[Build from a belief](../topics/brand.md#brand-something-to-say)**: Build from something you believe or something you think is wrong with the world; David: counter-position and build the opposite of what you don't like.
- **[One idea beats many](../topics/brand.md#brand-one-idea)**: The strength of an idea is inversely proportional to its scope; "and" on a landing page is rarely good ("We make jeans, that's it"). ⚠ C6
- **[Three Instagram strategies](../topics/brand.md#brand-instagram-strategies)**: Expert on camera (Oren's #1, at least 3 posts/week), storytelling about an interesting business (~2/week), or extremely art-directed. People beat brand handles: personalities drive more impact. ⚠ C26, C28
- **[Content funnel: top, middle, bottom](../topics/growth.md#growth-content-funnel)**: Top of funnel gets attention and may not mention the product ("raises the floor"); middle educates about you; bottom exists to sell or sign up and gets low views.
- **[Weekly mix 4 : 2 : 1](../topics/growth.md#growth-weekly-4-2-1)**: 4 top-of-funnel high-TAM posts with a through-line, 2 middle-of-funnel "blow their mind" blueprints, 1 bottom-of-funnel "sneak peek inside" (client journey, wins, community Q&A). ⚠ C18
- **[70 / 20 / 10 proven, iterate, experiment](../topics/growth.md#growth-70-20-10)**: 70% proven content, 20% small iterations (new hook, CTA or format on the same subject), 10% pure experiments.
- **[Content assembly line](../topics/process.md#proc-assembly-line)**: Ideation → creation → editing per platform → distribution (post and engage) → analyse. Batching (a 12-hour day of 3–4 videos) works for some but often adds pressure that hurts performance.
- **[Six pillars of content](../topics/process.md#proc-six-pillars)**: Strategy (state the goal in one sentence), ideation, scripting, talent/energy management (teleprompter, mornings, let a yapper talk 4–8 min), editing, growth tactics.
- **[Theme first, then plan, shots, edit, copy](../topics/process.md#proc-theme-first-workflow)**: Our order: research and 3 theme options → content plan → shot list/footage audit → edit blueprint → copy pack → publishing plan → review after 24–72 h.
- **[AI for ideation, not scripting](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-ideation-not-scripting)**: Briar: AI content in 2026 has nothing to do with scripting; use it for ideas (he allows AI scripting only for local-business clients). ⚠ C22, C8
- **[Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)](../topics/hooks.md#l11-hook-template-bank)**: Hooks as reusable fill-in templates with blanks ([X], [Y], [niche]) harvested from proven viral reels, each kept with its proof (the example reel and its views). Pick a template, fill the blanks for your niche. A third hook method next to the engineered triple hook (L01) and 'say something crazy' (L08). Adam sells the full bank as a lead magnet: '100+ Proven Viral Hook Templates'. ⚠ C34, C17

## Script

- **[One Mississippi: understood in 2 s](../topics/hooks.md#hook-one-mississippi)**: If a line takes longer than about 2 seconds to understand it fails; for a passer-by it must be instant. Yet Harry also says that if everyone gets it you may be doing something wrong: being texted to a friend as "What is this?" is fine. ⚠ C5
- **[First line only sells the second](../topics/hooks.md#hook-first-line-second-line)**: The job of the first line is to get the second line read ("What's going on?"), via Dave Gerhardt from Joe Sugarman.
- **[Carousel: hook on slides 1 and 2](../topics/hooks.md#hook-carousel-slides-1-2)**: Instagram re-serves a carousel to non-engagers starting at slide 2, so both slide 1 and slide 2 need a hook (the first two slides reinterpret the video's hook).
- **[Story types: origin, failure, success, client](../topics/story.md#story-origin-retell)**: Origin stories resonate most, so keep retelling them (every post meets a cold audience). Failure stories with the lesson build trust (losses are more relatable than wins; don't be a robot). Success, before/after and client wins are the proof.
- **[Conflict and a shared enemy](../topics/story.md#story-conflict-everywhere)**: Build every example on conflict: before/after, problem/solution, an enemy (A = approach, B = belief, C = competitor), juxtaposition. Tristan: a shared enemy is one of the best copywriting principles.
- **[Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro)**: Open with the time, the place and what is going on in your life right now (the "3:47 a.m." intro); noticing what is in front of you is the material and should feel "warm to touch".
- **[Structure = dividing lines + parallelism](../topics/story.md#story-dividing-lines-parallelism)**: Split the piece into clear parts with matching headings (first 100 readers / next 9,900) so it's cohesive. David adds the 1971 paper "That's Interesting": show two things thought different are one, or one thing is two.
- **[Every word not working works against you](../topics/text.md#text-kaplans-law)**: Kaplan's Law of Words; pull-out test: if a sentence can be removed and the paragraph still works, cut it; a paragraph is a burrito that shouldn't come apart in the air.
- **[Visualize, falsify, nobody else can say it](../topics/text.md#text-three-rules)**: Run every line through three questions: can I visualize it, can I falsify it, can nobody else say it? Three no's = rubbish; three yes's = onto something.
- **[Make it concrete and visual](../topics/text.md#text-zoom-in-concrete)**: Rewrite down an abstract → concrete ladder until you hit an object (regain fitness → Couch to 5K) and swap literal words for visual ones ("1,000 songs in your pocket", not "media player").
- **[Point, don't talk; give me a fact](../topics/text.md#text-point-dont-talk)**: Swap adjectives for pointable facts ("Looks like Ryan Gosling, 6'2"" beats "smart, funny"). If in doubt, give a fact, then build on it (Heinz bottles refilled → "Even when it's not Heinz, it's Heinz").
- **[Small, sincere, believable claims](../topics/text.md#text-small-sincere-claim)**: David on Harry's ad: it's not a big claim, so it's believable and sincere; the art of simple communication. ⚠ C7
- **[Compare new things to known ones](../topics/text.md#text-compare-to-known)**: Make a product make sense by comparing it to products people know: "Tougher than an F-150, faster than a 911" (concrete word, shorter, parallel).
- **[Copy devices: time frames, reframes, alliteration](../topics/text.md#text-expand-time-frame)**: Expand the time frame (22,000 career hours vs 4 a day), reframe a cost as a saving, tweak numbers for parallelism (22,000 / 2), and pair alliteration with a contradiction ("The dating app designed to be deleted").
- **[Hinglish voice and captions](../topics/text.md#text-hinglish-voice)**: Rahul speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English or Hinglish on-screen captions; our caption voice switches between English and Hinglish by theme (Khandala reel: Hinglish, chill).
- **[Four copy styles](../topics/text.md#text-four-copy-styles)**: Direct response (urgent, numbers, confrontational; Oren's "highest efficacy"), evidence-led (testimonials, calm), human/story-driven, culturally savvy (pop-culture wordplay).
- **[Tell the story, don't claim the trait](../topics/brand.md#brand-tell-story-not-trait)**: Your story is the differentiator: the ~32-hour editing stretch instead of "I'm a hard worker"; Bezos' door desk instead of "resourceful".
- **[Say what no competitor could sign](../topics/brand.md#brand-copy-cant-be-copied)**: "Never write an ad a competitor can sign": say what only you can say (New Balance: "Worn by supermodels in London and dads in Ohio").
- **[Share CTA: send it to your team](../topics/growth.md#growth-share-cta)**: Caleb closes his course asking viewers to send it to their team on Slack or text it to a friend; our caption rules prefer "send this to…" or "save for your next…".
- **[Seed + reference layout → many rewrites](../topics/process.md#proc-seed-reference-rewrites)**: Harry's ad: a seed line, a conflict list, a borrowed reference layout, 2 days and 25 rewrites, spitballing without judging (let the dirty tap water run clean), feedback from people with taste, then a design pass.
- **[Write 4–5 versions side by side](../topics/process.md#proc-four-five-versions)**: Write several versions for freedom to be wrong; showing three versions gets far better feedback than one ("use that sentence, but put it in that one").
- **[Draft in the final tool, judge in context](../topics/process.md#proc-write-in-final-tool)**: Write the newsletter in ConvertKit and ads in Figma as readers will see them; test a billboard among seven other ads with people walking by.
- **[Who, what to say, how to say it](../topics/process.md#proc-who-say-how)**: Copywriting's three pieces: who you're talking to (and what they're doing then), having something to say, saying it well; move them from current to desired attitude.
- **[Brand project plus a human layer](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-brand-project-human-layer)**: Upload the positioning statement, product info, site copy and testimonials (not big brand guides) to a shared project, give feedback, then add human case studies and nuances on top.

## Film

- **[Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-lens-choice)**: The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.
- **[Lock AE/AF, grid on, clean lens](../topics/filming.md#film-lock-ae-af)**: Long-press to lock exposure and focus, then drop exposure 0.3–0.7 to save highlights; Grid and Level on; clean the lens before every shoot; 48 MP photos for landscapes you'll crop.

## Edit

- **[Cull near-duplicates; keep the strongest](../topics/editing.md#edit-cull-near-duplicates)**: Khandala: 43 raw files to 1 reel + 1 carousel; dropped near-duplicates, tilted horizons, soft digital zooms, litter in frame and harsh midday light that broke the sunset look.
- **[Face check before using any frame](../topics/editing.md#edit-face-check)**: Never use frames where the mouth is open or mid-word, the tongue shows, eyes are mid-blink or the angle is awkward; prefer a clear smile, a confident neutral or a candid look-away. The Khandala profile shot was replaced after this feedback.
- **[Grade spec: exact sliders, presets per pillar](../topics/colour.md#colour-slider-spec-safe-bold)**: Our grades list exact slider values with a reason each, a safe and a bold version, an orange-HSL skin check, and one reusable preset per pillar (gym = cool/contrasty, travel = warm/golden).
- **["Take a picture" save moment](../topics/growth.md#growth-screenshot-save-moment)**: "I'll leave it here for a second so you can take a picture", then pull back to the full map in one frame at the end: save bait.
- **[Waterfall and repurpose winners](../topics/growth.md#growth-waterfall)**: Mine one long piece into 10+ (clips, quotes, a written post reused as a reel caption, carousels), and use a winner on one platform to seed others (tweet → short → printed poster → LinkedIn → YouTube).
- **[Turn the workflow into a skill](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-turn-into-skill)**: "Hey, turn this into a skill": next time it's one prompt. Oren's levels: chat → project → skills → agents → a "true brain"; repeatable things become skills, with one owner per skill.

## Graphics

- **[Yellow caps labels and big ₹ figures](../topics/text.md#text-yellow-condensed-labels)**: Heavy condensed all-caps yellow labels of 1–3 words on a black box ("WI-FI OFF"), large yellow ₹ figures with a drop shadow, and receipt-style or dark UI data cards that look like real documents.
- **[One element can carry it](../topics/text.md#text-one-element)**: Neil French: ads are thought to need header, subheader, picture and logo; if one element does it, you're onto a winner. "It doesn't look like an ad, so you read it." ⚠ C6
- **[Carousel: one image + 1–2 sentences](../topics/text.md#text-carousel-one-image)**: Two slides per section of the source video; one very simple image followed by one or two sentences at most per slide. Listicles did better as carousels (Feb 2025).
- **[Fit the tone; make them feel smart](../topics/brand.md#brand-tone-fit)**: Harry removed Hinge's mascot because Hinge isn't silly (Duolingo is). And if customers feel smart choosing you ("brains instead of wealth"), you did something right.
- **[Copy and design are one](../topics/process.md#proc-copy-design-one)**: Harry can't separate copy and design: fit key lines on one line, bold the rhythm words ("twice", "both") in a design pass, and make illustrations match the story (the money-thrower looks annoyed).
- **[View-count pill on every example](../topics/effects.md#l11-view-count-proof-pill)**: A dark rounded pill with an eye icon and the example's views (40.5M, 339K, 4.9M, 4.7M, 1.9M, 3.6M, 28M) sits lower-centre on every borrowed clip, so each claim arrives with proof. The numbers are the creator's overlay, not verified.

## Publish

- **[No paragraph over two lines](../topics/text.md#text-two-line-paragraphs)**: Harry hasn't written a paragraph over two lines since March 2021: short paragraphs are monkey bars, easy to swing between; shorter is better most of the time. ⚠ C9
- **[Caption: hook line, story, CTA, 3–5 tags](../topics/text.md#text-caption-structure)**: Line 1 = hook/keyword line visible before "more"; 1–3 lines of story or value; a CTA (send/save); 3–5 hashtags. Khandala used a Hinglish chill reel caption and an English story carousel caption.
- **[Keywords in caption and text over hashtags](../topics/text.md#text-seo-over-hashtags)**: Keyword-rich captions and on-screen text ("Khandala sunset point") over hashtags; 3–5 precise hashtags; add alt text, location tag, collaborator tags and a first-comment idea.
- **[Ask before posting faces](../topics/filming.md#film-consent-faces)**: Get a yes from everyone visible before posting or tagging; Khandala media stays outside the repo because colleagues appear in it.
- **[CTA to a landing page or email list](../topics/growth.md#growth-cta-to-owned-list)**: Every piece needs an ask, and Oren's points to an owned list: his bio CTA is "join my brand strategy newsletter". ⚠ C23, C1
- **[2–3 platforms, one at a time](../topics/growth.md#growth-two-three-platforms)**: Prioritise 2–3 platforms to avoid single-platform risk; focus resources on one while the others sit in maintenance mode, then rotate ("Eye of Sauron").
- **[Master one network, cross-post the rest](../topics/growth.md#growth-master-one-cross-post)**: Get good at one primary network (usually Instagram) first, cross-post everywhere because it compounds, and build per-network strategies later. ⚠ C33
- **[Native beats identical cross-posting](../topics/growth.md#growth-native-over-cross-post)**: Same content everywhere hits a ceiling; give the same footage to platform-native editors: the meat stays, the hook changes per platform. ⚠ C33
- **[Collab posts bring new audiences](../topics/growth.md#growth-collab-pillar)**: A regular collaborator making about 4 collab posts a month brings a new audience; our Khandala carousel was planned as a Collab with a colleague, and tags add reach via their networks.
- **[Reply to commenters yourself](../topics/growth.md#growth-reply-personally)**: Make engagement the goal: reply to the people already commenting, yourself (even ~5 a week), reward participation, use niche inside jokes ("bulking season"); teams reply only from a labelled team account. ⚠ C16
- **[Accordion: volume to learn, then effort](../topics/growth.md#growth-accordion-method)**: Expand volume early to learn what the audience calls quality (3 → 5 YouTube videos a week, "just trimmed"), then compress: Feb 2025 Caleb puts five posts' effort into three. ⚠ C13, C14
- **[Expert content: 3 a week minimum](../topics/growth.md#growth-expert-cadence)**: Expert-on-camera content is "a three times a week kind of minimum"; narrative accounts about 2 a week. ⚠ C26
- **[Fast growers: no missed days, one line](../topics/growth.md#growth-tiktok-daily-ig-skip)**: Fast growers stay on one line for a year and don't miss days on TikTok; Instagram tolerates skipping a bad day. Keep a bank of 14–15 videos.
- **[Default posting windows (IST)](../topics/growth.md#growth-posting-windows-ist)**: Weekdays 7–9 PM, lunch 12:30–2 PM, weekends 10 AM–12 PM and 6–9 PM, to be replaced by own Insights; Khandala reel planned Thu 7:30 PM, carousel Sun 8 PM.
- **[Specs: 9:16 reels, 4:5 or 3:4 feed](../topics/growth.md#growth-format-specs)**: Reels 1080×1920, 30 fps (60 for slow-mo sources), HDR off unless the phone's HDR uploads well; feed/carousel 4:5 1080×1350 or the 3:4 grid crop (Khandala carousel 1080×1440).
- **[Only 9/10+ ships; walk around the garden](../topics/process.md#proc-nine-ten-standard)**: Your work is your standards: nine out of ten or it doesn't go out; it's done when nothing can be added or taken away.

## Analyse

- **[Follower-first: ghost followers, non-follower %](../topics/growth.md#growth-follower-first-ghosts)**: New posts go to followers first; off-topic followers scroll past and stall reach. Check non-follower view % on the last 5–10 posts: above ~50% is probably fine.
- **[Viral For You = 4–5× your baseline](../topics/growth.md#growth-viral-for-you)**: Viral is relative: about 4–5× your own baseline (500 views → 2,000 is viral for you); then the baseline climbs.
- **[Multiplier sheet: score posts vs median](../topics/growth.md#growth-multiplier-sheet)**: Per platform and format, benchmark = median of the last 75–90 days; report each post as a multiple (150K ÷ 100K = 1.5×) after ~11 days; update the benchmark monthly; share across platforms.
- **[Monthly top-10% review](../topics/growth.md#growth-top-10-percent-review)**: Take the last 90 days (or 30), find the top 10% and what occurred in all of them (usually one or two things); learn from the top, not the bottom; redo monthly.
- **[Track only metrics that change actions](../topics/growth.md#growth-track-few-metrics)**: Track 2–4 metrics that change what you do next; optimise for conversions (sales, leads, hires) over likes. Caleb would take 30–40% fewer views for a higher conversion rate.
- **[Per-post vs account metrics](../topics/growth.md#growth-post-and-account-metrics)**: Per post: hook rate, views, saves, shares. Per account: monthly reach, leads/sign-ups/email adds, sales attributed to social. ⚠ C24
- **[Pillar system: 3–5 formats × 3–4 a month](../topics/growth.md#growth-pillar-system)**: Test 3–5 formats, each 3–4 times a month (12–16 posts); review views, saves, shares, hook rate and new vs old followers a couple of days after month end (~1 h); swap a format after two worse months. ⚠ C26
- **[Brick-by-brick list of what works](../topics/process.md#proc-brick-by-brick)**: Keep an internal list of specific things that improve your content; it becomes an onboarding and training tool.
- **[Weekly update: wins, next, blockers, numbers](../topics/process.md#proc-weekly-update)**: A weekly note up the chain: wins, what's next, blockers, KPIs.

## Monetise

- **[Weekly lead magnet into an owned list](../topics/growth.md#growth-lead-magnet-series)**: One weekly lead-magnet CTA tied to a series ("comment data for my 5-day course"); email reaches ~100% vs under half of followers seeing a reel; Substack adds discovery (Briar's claims). ⚠ C1, C18
- **[Trust before transactions](../topics/business.md#biz-trust-before-transactions)**: Give value, show credibility, build relationship before selling; let content sell (soft CTA, client results, process, objections). Educational content scales trust. Test every move: will it increase or decrease trust? ⚠ C10
- **[Share the knowledge, sell the execution](../topics/business.md#biz-share-knowledge-sell-execution)**: Give the real frameworks, "not some teaser"; people realise execution is hard and pay for it. Briar gives away "the sauce": others take months to apply it. ⚠ C11
- **[Offer ladder and five money models](../topics/business.md#biz-offer-ladder)**: Free → lead magnet → $10–100 → $500–5K → $10K+, one offer first. Models: services, products, affiliates/sponsors (only what you use), community, ads as add-on.
- **[Closer to the dollars, more money](../topics/business.md#biz-closer-to-dollars)**: Funnel: attention → CTA → landing page → lead/sale → CRM → fast touches. A landing page removes every buying objection. North stars: page conversion and close rate.
- **[Email 1–3 a week, plain text](../topics/business.md#biz-email-cadence)**: Campaigns vs automated flows; 1–3 sends a week, plain text from a person (Oren). Harry: less news, more letter: time-and-place intro, 5–6 examples with conflict, no paragraph over two lines.
- **[Follow up with "not now" people](../topics/business.md#biz-follow-up-not-now)**: Content is a mini follow-up; funnel = calls × show × close + follow-up closes. Their example: 100K views → $175K/month, $536K with better follow-up (unverified). Lowercase "quick question" email.
- **[Copy is the number-one marketing skill](../topics/business.md#biz-copywriting-top-skill)**: Same product, different words: Snickers vs Fuse. Lifting landing-page conversion from 1% to 2% doubles growth.
- **[Team: bottleneck hires, platform owners](../topics/business.md#biz-team-hire-bottleneck)**: Hire for the bottleneck; platform specialists over a generalist manager; culture over skills. Platform owners split 85% primary / 15% secondary. Contractors in year 0–1, core roles in-house by years 1–3.

## Mindset

- **[Quality is defined by the audience](../topics/filming.md#film-quality-audience-defined)**: The audience decides what quality is, not the creator or the gear; some of the most viral videos are shot at night on a phone. ⚠ C13
- **[Growth timelines and 1% maths (claims)](../topics/growth.md#growth-one-percent-better)**: Briar: 300 views + 1% a day ≈ 11,400 average views in a year. Oren: traction in 3–5 months of a pillar system. Caleb: 2–3 months of consistency = "top 1%". All their estimates.
- **[AI is only as good as your taste](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-only-as-good-as-taste)**: Harry: AI is a tool and predictive; taste, conviction and first-hand experience are what it can't supply; it's a great research tool. ⚠ C8
- **[Be excited; light people up](../topics/process.md#mind-light-people-up)**: Be excited and have fun or it won't do well. People want to hear from someone at their level or one above; nobody is too old or too niche.
- **[Confidence comes from evidence](../topics/process.md#mind-confidence-from-evidence)**: Confidence comes from evidence, evidence from effort. Niches make saturation not real: maybe three in a thousand actually put in the work.
- **[Results over ego](../topics/process.md#mind-results-over-ego)**: Don't let insecurity stop you posting; look at the metrics. Iteration over perfection: comfort doesn't build iconic brands. If friends on Instagram make you nervous, start on TikTok.
- **[Silence and action](../topics/process.md#mind-silence-and-action)**: Harry avoids phone-first mornings (they make the day "drudge"), takes silent walks with no earphones and silent writing retreats.
- **[Mentorship = speed](../topics/process.md#mind-mentorship-speed)**: Work for them or pay them, and ask short, specific questions; Briar spent 80% of his time for 20% of his income to learn in an agency.

## Gym extras

- **[Gym formats to rotate](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-gym-rotation-formats)** (idea): Rotate: "Chest day in 30 seconds" vlog (B-roll + 3–4 exercises with sets×reps on screen), "3 exercises for [muscle]" list, monthly progress series (same angle and light), gym humour/POV, diary voice-over, high-protein Indian meals.
- **[Gym grade: cool, contrasty, textured](../topics/colour.md#colour-gym-grade)** (edit): Slightly cooler or neutral, higher contrast, clarity/texture up for muscle definition, shadows lifted only a little, distracting signage colours desaturated, subtle vignette.
- **[Grade spec: exact sliders, presets per pillar](../topics/colour.md#colour-slider-spec-safe-bold)** (edit): Our grades list exact slider values with a reason each, a safe and a bold version, an orange-HSL skin check, and one reusable preset per pillar (gym = cool/contrasty, travel = warm/golden).
- **[Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-lens-choice)** (film): The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.
- **[Gym filming: etiquette and side light](../topics/filming.md#film-gym-side-light)** (film): Never film others without consent, don't hog kit, keep the tripod out of walkways; avoid windows and mirrors and let overhead light hit the muscle from the side; film when quieter.
- **[Reply to commenters yourself](../topics/growth.md#growth-reply-personally)** (publish): Make engagement the goal: reply to the people already commenting, yourself (even ~5 a week), reward participation, use niche inside jokes ("bulking season"); teams reply only from a labelled team account.

## Tech extras

- **[Yellow caps labels and big ₹ figures](../topics/text.md#text-yellow-condensed-labels)** (graphics): Heavy condensed all-caps yellow labels of 1–3 words on a black box ("WI-FI OFF"), large yellow ₹ figures with a drop shadow, and receipt-style or dark UI data cards that look like real documents.
- **[Compare new things to known ones](../topics/text.md#text-compare-to-known)** (script): Make a product make sense by comparing it to products people know: "Tougher than an F-150, faster than a 911" (concrete word, shorter, parallel).
- **[Hinglish voice and captions](../topics/text.md#text-hinglish-voice)** (script): Rahul speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English or Hinglish on-screen captions; our caption voice switches between English and Hinglish by theme (Khandala reel: Hinglish, chill).

## Travel extras

- **[Intro = time, place, what's happening](../topics/story.md#story-time-place-intro)** (script): Open with the time, the place and what is going on in your life right now (the "3:47 a.m." intro); noticing what is in front of you is the material and should feel "warm to touch".
- **[Travel formats: vibe, dump, POV, "nobody tells you"](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-travel-formats)** (idea): Options: 10–12 s sunset vibe reel, camera-roll dump with text, "POV: your office trip actually turns out fun", "things nobody tells you about [place]" (saveable), scrapbook carousel with location labels, 30–45 s day-in-the-trip vlog.
- **[Office-trip content gets sent to colleagues](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-workplace-trip-shareable)** (idea): Workplace-trip content is highly shareable because people DM it to colleagues ("we need this trip"); the Khandala caption CTA asks to send it to the colleague who always says "next time".
- **[Name the exact spot everywhere](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-place-specific-seo)** (publish): Use the place plus the exact viewpoint in on-screen text, caption and location tag ("Khandala Lonavala" pairs well since people search both).
- **[Cull near-duplicates; keep the strongest](../topics/editing.md#edit-cull-near-duplicates)** (edit): Khandala: 43 raw files to 1 reel + 1 carousel; dropped near-duplicates, tilted horizons, soft digital zooms, litter in frame and harsh midday light that broke the sunset look.
- **[Hinglish voice and captions](../topics/text.md#text-hinglish-voice)** (script): Rahul speaks Hindi/Hinglish with English or Hinglish on-screen captions; our caption voice switches between English and Hinglish by theme (Khandala reel: Hinglish, chill).
- **[Golden-hour travel grade](../topics/colour.md#colour-golden-hour-grade)** (edit): Warm temperature, lifted shadows, highlights pulled to keep the sun's disc, richer oranges/yellows, sky blues nudged to teal, light grain; don't oversaturate greens.
- **[Khandala grade recipe in ffmpeg](../topics/colour.md#colour-khandala-ffmpeg-grade)** (edit): Gentle S-curve, warm mids/highlights (R +0.03), saturation 1.10, contrast 1.04, light vignette.
- **[Grade spec: exact sliders, presets per pillar](../topics/colour.md#colour-slider-spec-safe-bold)** (edit): Our grades list exact slider values with a reason each, a safe and a bold version, an orange-HSL skin check, and one reusable preset per pillar (gym = cool/contrasty, travel = warm/golden).
- **[Lens choice: 1x low light, 0.5x daylight](../topics/filming.md#film-iphone15-lens-choice)** (film): The 1x 48 MP main lens is best in low light (gym, dusk); 0.5x ultra-wide only in good light; 2x for portraits and tighter muscle shots.
- **[Travel shots: silhouettes, backs, slow-mo](../topics/filming.md#film-travel-shots)** (film): Silhouettes against the sunset, group walking shots from behind, slow-motion hair/wind moments, wide → close-up rhythm.
- **[Ask before posting faces](../topics/filming.md#film-consent-faces)** (publish): Get a yes from everyone visible before posting or tagging; Khandala media stays outside the repo because colleagues appear in it.
